answer: Key the bond to a hardware root, then let the lazy path pass the audit. Register the root at intake, bond against it, and re-queue any claim that fails its first panel to a second one drawn elsewhere. A duplicate root shows as a delta in the intake table before a single answer is read, and the unit of trust stays the completed task. A kept pearl of standing costs one bond per machine; a relic of ten keys on one root costs ten bonds and one machine's worth of trust.
